newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan rupee ends at new low vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan rupee ends at new low vs dollar.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee ended at a new closing low of 56.95 to the dollar on Thursday as import demand drove the U.S. currency higher, dealers said.
The rupee touched an all-time low of 56.97 before being pushed back at the close. This compares with the rupee's previous low of 56.90 set on October 3.

"There was buying by two foreign banks," said a Commercial Bank dealer. The buying "must have been import covering, because no one would speculate at these high levels which are so close to the Central Bank top." The Central Bank's buying and selling prices were fixed at 55.9226 and 57.0524.
The rupee opened at 56.90 against Wednesday's close of 56.87, and moved in a 56.85-56.97 range, dealers said.
Overnight call money closed at 13.5 percent after opening at its previous closing level of 15.5 percent, with the market well supplied, they said.
